provenance.finalKey: cuet-2026-final-keys.pdf (NTA CUET (UG) 2026 final answer key), subject 322, 26 shifts (24 x 50 rows, one 49, one 48); rows extracted to tmp/1123-papers/physics/work/keys-physics.json

structure: Group 8 'Physics' (60 minutes, 250 marks), one mandatory section of 50 numbered questions (391 to 440), all stand-alone MCQs, each printed in English then Hindi. The header says 'Number of Questions: 50', 'to be attempted: 50' and 'Section Marks: 250'. No comprehension passage.
authentication: A question is authenticated when its printed NTA question id is in the 24-05-2026 (Second) final key for subject 322 and the key option id is one of its four printed option ids. Printed question ids run consecutively (226895791657 for Q391 to 226895791706 for Q440) and option ids run consecutively, four per question.
notes: Each question is printed in English, then Hindi; only the English is transcribed, read from the page images. Spelling and wording kept as printed (e.g. Q401 'At what temperature the resistance', Q412 'Identity the correct statement(s)', Q430 'Plank's constant', Q437 'valance band' in option 2, Q440 'distance of closet approach').

Notation: powers are written with ^ (10^-6, r^2), subscripts as plain characters (C1, μ0, ε0, n2), fractions with / ; Q439 prints the nucleus as a superscript 235 over a subscript 92 before U, written here as ^235_92U. Q433 prints the nuclides as '4He', '6Li', '14N', '12C' (mass number, then the symbol set low), kept as printed.
Page = the PDF page (pNN of the 43-page PDF; the printed footer is one lower) where the question's English option ids were read.
Match tables are written as rows 'List-I item | List-II item' in the order the paper prints them.
Q409 has a figure; it is described in words in the stem (three-quarter circular arc of radius 3 cm round O, with straight leads along two radii at 90 degrees).

Q407: the English stem gives the flux density as 2.52 x 10^-3 T; the Hindi copy prints 2.5 x 10^-3 T. The English is transcribed; NTA's key gives option 2 (2.0 A), which fits both (B = μ0 n I with n = 1000 per m gives 2.0 A).
Q424: the options print bare numbers (1/2, 1, 1/4, 1/3) without the factor I; kept as printed. NTA's key gives option 3 (1/4), i.e. I/4.
Q397: option 4 prints '6 × 10^6 J' (positive exponent) as printed.
Q438: the key gives option 3 (A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I), which fits n_e = doping concentration and n_h = n_i^2 / n_e with the printed numbers.

OCR missed the English header line of 12 questions (395, 396, 401, 402, 419, 420, 422, 423, 429, 430, 432, 440); their question ids and option ids were read from the page images and checked against the Hindi copy, the consecutive id runs and the OCR option-id lines; they then authenticated like the rest.
Every key was read against NCERT physics and fits the English text as transcribed; none needed a note beyond those above.

The shift's key has 50 rows, all single-answer, none dropped. NTA's final key for subject 322 holds 26 shifts; this paper is the 24-05-2026 Second shift and all 50 question ids fall in that one shift.
OCR slips fixed: none needed in the final text, because the text was typed from the page images, not cleaned from OCR (the OCR draft dropped spaces and broke formulas, and was used only for ids).
